SQL skills to highlight

SELECTWHEREORDER BYJOININSERTUPDATEStored ProceduresFiltering

Keep only the SQL topics you can explain confidently in an interview. The example below is a generic practice example, not company SQL.

Example: filter inventory records
-- Practice example only; use your actual schema when testing.
SELECT
    Block,
    Lot,
    Phase,
    LotType,
    LotArea,
    Status
FROM LotInventory
WHERE ProjectName = @ProjectName
  AND (@Status IS NULL OR Status = @Status)
ORDER BY Block, Lot;

This illustrates selecting inventory fields, filtering by project and optional status, and sorting the results.

How I use SQL in an application

  1. The user selects a filter or enters search details.
  2. The controller or application code passes the values to a query or stored procedure.
  3. SQL Server returns the matching records.
  4. The application displays the results in a grid or report, or exports them to Excel.
